newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds soften ahead of Tues FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds soften ahead of Tues FOMC meeting.

text.p: Argentine bonds were softer Friday in a dull market focused on the Tuesday meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee that will set the course of U.S. interest rate policy.
"Eight out of 12 Federal Reserve governors have said the FOMC may raise rates 1/4 point and that upset the bond market," a bond dealer for a large Argentine bank said.
Any hike in U.S. rates could knock down U.S. Treasuries and in turn push Argentine bonds lower.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.31 to 117.49, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 declined 1/8 to 82-3/8.
"It looks like there is some shift from bonds to stocks, which are firmer," a dealer for another large local bank said. "There are some worries about what course of action the Fed will take."
"In the short-term, bonds may stay around these levels or slightly below, but we are optmistic for the mid-term as the government has regained economic initiative."
Shares firmed today, catching up after lagging gains in bonds since President Carlos Menem fired Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo at the end of July, and there is more room to rise, dealers say.
